findings.summary: If the process dies before the commit, the recovered invocation record has no `reading_attempt`.
findings.evidence: I read `invoke_and_record`: it builds the record and calls `self.state.write_live(...)` before returning it to `read_once`. The plan sets `record.reading_attempt` only afterwards, in memory. If the process dies before `invocation_files` commits, `athena close` commits the live copy (manage.rs:249). That copy has no field, so the refusal drops out of the counts without any sign. Fix: After setting `reading_attempt` in `read_once`, write the live copy again: `self.state.write_live(job, &any.canonical_path(), any.to_json().as_bytes())`. Alternatively, note in docs/records.md that an interrupted read may have no `reading_attempt`.

findings.summary: Rules that never refused are not listed, but criterion 7 says each reading rule is listed with its two counts.
findings.evidence: Criterion 7 reads: 'The diff in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs shows each reading rule listed with its two counts.' Decision 7 lists only rules that refused at least once. A verifier reading the criterion strictly could fail it. The worry that a full list would drift is answerable: refusal_corpus.rs:2701 already parses the `step!` lines of `refusing_check` from source, so the same kind of test could pin a name list to them. Fix: Either list every rule, using a `pub const` of check names (the `refusing_check` steps plus `check_reading_size` and `other`) pinned by a test against the `step!` lines, so unused rules show 0 / 0. Or have `text()` print a line saying rules not listed refused nothing in the window, and say so in the criterion 7 evidence.

findings.summary: Grouping by exact text makes 'most common refusal text' almost always a count of 1, so it is really the latest example.
findings.evidence: Refusal texts include values specific to each reading. For example, `check_reading_size` puts the forecast p50 into its text (reading.rs:367), and other checks quote paths and criterion text. The plan admits that ties at 1 will be common and breaks them by recency. The flag would then name 'the most common text' when that text occurred once. Fix: Keep exact grouping, but when the top count is 1 the evidence should say so ('no text repeated; latest example: ...') rather than calling it most common. A further option is to mask quoted or backticked spans and digits before grouping. That only affects measurement, not any rule.

findings.summary: The demonstrations and dependents cite the wrong step numbers.
findings.evidence: The demonstrations say `compute` comes from 'plan step 2' and `reading_rule_findings`/`ReadingRulesCheck` from 'plan step 5'. The Steps list puts them at 5, 7 and 8. The docs/records.md dependent says 'step 8 adds a paragraph', but that is step 9. Fix: Change the cross-references to match the Steps list.

summary: I read the code the plan names and checked its claims against it. The plan is sound and puts the fix where the fault starts. Today nothing records which rule refused a reading. In reading.rs, `read_once` (line 555) turns the gate's result into a plain `ReadError::Refused(String)`, which drops the rule's name. The function the plan switches to, `refusing_check` (checks.rs:518), already returns that name, using `stringify!`. Adding an optional `reading_attempt` field to `Invocation` (records.rs:691, `deny_unknown_fields`, with `effort` as a precedent) is the smallest place to keep the result. It is right to put it there and not on `Reading`, because a reading refused twice leaves no Reading record (run_pin_tests.rs:2011), while both of its invocations are committed through `invocation_files`. Every place the plan relies on exists: the `Invocation` struct literals it lists (my grep found no others), the single `StatusView` literal (status.rs:1071), `STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS` and its test (status.rs:1405), the `hestia_sweep_with`/`hestia_sweep_measuring`/`hestia_sweep` chain (hestia.rs:2655-2718), the pinned count of 3 ui lines (hestia.rs:4728), and `default_checks()` being empty. The only production caller of `hestia_sweep_with` is commands.rs:201, and no CLI test runs a sweep. Wrapping `check_reading_acceptance` does not trip `no_check_bypasses_refusing_check`, because that test only scans the wrapper's body. Each demonstration uses a real seam: `compute`/`Athena::status()`, `reading_rule_findings`/`run_sweep`/`hestia_sweep_with`, and the scripted-reader tests in run_pin_tests.rs. Each would fail without the behavior. The dependents list covers every reader I found. The plan calls no external service and is not a landing plan. I found only minor issues. (1) The live copy of the invocation is written before the field is set, so if the process crashes, the recovered record has no `reading_attempt`. (2) Rules that never refused are left out, which a strict reading of criterion 7 could fault. (3) Grouping refusal text by exact match will mostly produce counts of 1. (4) The demonstrations point to the wrong step numbers.
